The '''1999–2000 [[La Liga]]''' season, the 69th since its establishment. It began on 21 August 1999, and concluded on 20 May 2000. [[Deportivo de La Coruña|Deportivo La Coruña]] won a first La Liga title with 69 points, the lowest for a champion since the [[three points for a win]] rule was introduced in 1995.<ref>{{cite news |last=Sochon |first=Mark |date=12 February 2016 |title=When La Liga was just as unpredictable as this season's Premier League |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/these-football-times/2016/feb/12/la-liga-unpedictable-league-deportivo-barcelona-real-madrid |work=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref>

== Promotion and relegation ==
Twenty teams competed in the league&nbsp;– the top sixteen teams from the previous season and the four teams promoted from the [[1998–99 Segunda División|Segunda División]]. The promoted teams were [[Málaga CF|Málaga]], [[CD Numancia|Numancia]], [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] and [[Rayo Vallecano]]. Sevilla and Rayo Vallecano returned to the top flight after an absence of two years while Málaga CF and Numancia were promoted for the first time. However, since CD Málaga played in the [[1989–90 La Liga]], the city of Málaga returned to the top fight after an absence of nine years. They replaced [[CF Extremadura|Extremadura]], [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]] (both teams relegated after a season's presence), [[CD Tenerife|Tenerife]] (ending their top flight spell of eleven years) and [[UD Salamanca|Salamanca]] (ending their top flight spell of two years).

=== Fair Play award ===
[[Rayo Vallecano]] was the winner of the Fair-play award with 102 points;<ref name="FairPlay">{{cite web|title=Ganadores de los Premios Juego Limpio |trans-title=Fair-play awards Winners |url=http://www.rfef.es/index.jsp?nodo=298#ancla7 |publisher=[[Royal Spanish Football Federation|RFEF]] |access-date=5 September 2010 |language=Spanish |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100407195555/http://www.rfef.es/index.jsp?nodo=298 |archive-date=7 April 2010 }}</ref> moreover, it was elected on 8 June 2000 in [[Brussels]] as one of the three entries by UEFA to enter [[2000–01 UEFA Cup#Qualifying round|UEFA Cup in the qualifying round]] by the same [[UEFA Cup#History|condition]] of Fair Play.

* <small>Source: [[El Mundo Deportivo (newspaper)|El Mundo Deportivo]] (newspaper archive, web)<ref>{{cite web|title=El Rayo, a Europa la próxima temporada |trans-title=Rayo, to Europe next season |url=http://hemeroteca.elmundodeportivo.es/preview/2000/06/09/pagina-41/1481449/pdf.html |publisher=[[El Mundo Deportivo (newspaper)|El Mundo Deportivo]] |date=9 July 2000 |access-date=5 September 2010 |language=Spanish}}</ref></small>
